evals.name: nextjs-saas-greenfield
evals.prompt: We're a 12-person B2B SaaS shipping a Next.js + Prisma + Postgres app to mid-market customers in the EU and US. No analytics yet. Leadership wants to know which features are actually used so we can cut the bottom 20% in next quarter's planning, and the growth lead wants signup funnel attribution from paid channels. Plan our GA4 instrumentation. The repo is open in your working directory.
evals.expected_output: A two-artifact deliverable: (a) a design plan in docs/agents/features/PLANNED-ga4-instrumentation.md with 3–7 named decisions, an architecture choice with rejected alternatives, a closed event catalog with file:line anchors, a consent plan that deny-defaults in EU, hashed+peppered user_id, registered custom dimensions/metrics + units, and a verification checklist; and (b) a runbook in a sibling artifact covering the GA4 admin click-paths, custom-definition registration table, Consent Mode v2 defaults snippet, and DebugView validation. Should NOT propose ecommerce events, sGTM, or BigQuery — none are justified at this scale.

evals.name: django-server-only-with-children
evals.prompt: Our product is a homework-help app for K-12 students. Django backend, React Native client. We need to add analytics to understand which subjects are most used and which onboarding step kids drop off at. Most of our users are under 13. Build the plan.
evals.expected_output: The skill should ESCALATE before producing a plan: this is COPPA territory and a templated plan is unsafe. The response should name the regulatory issue (COPPA under 13, possibly state-level FERPA exposure if school-distributed), require parental-consent flow + server-side hard disable + counsel sign-off, and only after those guardrails are explicit propose what a minimal GA4 plan could look like. Should NOT propose Google Signals or ads features. Should NOT silently produce a normal plan.

evals.name: rails-ecommerce-with-existing-ga
evals.prompt: We already have GA4 on our Rails + Stripe ecommerce site via the gtag.js snippet in our layout. Ad-blocker rate is high; we estimate we're missing 20–30% of purchases vs Stripe's truth. Marketing is asking us to 'add server-side analytics'. We have a small ops team (2 engineers). Plan it.
evals.expected_output: The plan should explicitly compare the three architecture options (gtag.js direct, server-side Measurement Protocol from a Rails background job on purchase webhooks, full sGTM container) and recommend Measurement Protocol — not sGTM — because the team size and the specific gap (purchase data) doesn't justify sGTM infra. Plan should specify: minting client_id from the _ga cookie at purchase, idempotent transaction_id, full ecommerce items[] payload, ISO-4217 currency, the queue/worker pattern with drop-on-overflow, and a debug-endpoint validation step. Should call out the modeled-conversion-loss tradeoff and document the rollback path.
